items.item_text: Bachelor’s degree in related field.
2-4 years of relevant experience.

Experience communicating effectively and professionally and working with a variety of internal and external partners, including UCLA administrators, outside funders, policy makers and community representatives.

As a key member of the Department of Medicine Advisory & Compliance unit, you will provide critical analytical and administrative support to the UCLA David Geffen School of Medicine and its 18+ Divisions. Position will involve providing system access, reviewing transactions, analyzing key indicators, and recommending actionable steps to maintain compliance. The position will require an understanding of University policies and procedures related to access, procurement/material management, accounting, human resources, and laboratory safety. You will provide high-level summary reports for leadership and communicate with division constituents to improve compliance.
We’re seeking the ideal independent, detail-oriented candidate with:
Computer proficiency with MS Office and particular expertise with Excel to generate charts/graphs and pivot tables to summarize large data sets
Demonstrate skill with Adobe Acrobat, DocuSign, and various internet utilities
Exceptional mathematical and analytical abilities
Strong communication, interpersonal, and collaboration skills
Expertise with online systems used to generate reports and ensure compliance
Skill in organizing material and information in a systemic and accurate way

the final candidate who accepts an offer of employment will be required to disclose if they have been subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct; or have filed an appeal of a finding of substantiated misconduct with a previous employer.
Ability to work independently and also have interpersonal skills to work with teams.
Demonstrated writing skills to produce wide range of documents and deliverables.
Working knowledge of evaluation, creating datasets, grant writing and proposal submission.

Strong organizational skills to successfully work on and track complex programs involving short deadlines and multiple tasks, in coordination with multiple teams to achieve program/project mission and goals.

Working knowledge of program/project development, evaluation, creating datasets, financial management and reporting, research principles including CITI training, grant writing and proposal submission, University procedures and policies, program/project related federal and state regulations.
Ability to seek out and learn new policies, procedures, and software to advance the mission of the program/project.
Ability to train new program/project managers and other staff within and external to the unit.
May be subject to test in qualifying skills**
